# Coins on different surfaces

<!-- STEP id="wood" -->
Tape four 10-rupee coins into a stack. Stretch a rubber band a little between your finger and thumb, and mark its ends A and B. Push the stack back against the band to a mark C, then let go. On a wooden table top, the stack slides and stops.

<!-- STEP id="surfaces" -->
Do the same, with the same stretch, on a laminated table top, then on a polished marble floor. The stack goes farther each time. Its velocity falls more slowly.

<!-- STEP id="forces" -->
While the band pushes it, the push is larger than friction. A net force acts forward, and the stack speeds up. Once it leaves the band, only friction acts on it, opposite to its motion, and it slows down to rest.
